title: inline label filter (v7) — recall vs M87 post-filter at ~1% selectivity

dataset.note: well-separated clusters (unambiguous neighbors; recall meaningful, unlike M88 tie-dense)

ground_truth: exact seqscan-filtered top-10 (WHERE lbl && '{L}' ORDER BY e <-> q LIMIT 10)

correctness.note: every index-scan filtered row satisfies the predicate (inline skip + xs_recheck); v5/v6/vector-only byte-identical (v7 opt-in on 2nd column)

boundary: only the declared label column + && (smallint[]); arbitrary-WHERE inline is M91 (Custom Scan Provider, Approach B)
format v7 + REINDEX to use labels; label-less indexes unaffected (no REINDEX)
NOT a QPS-superiority claim vs ScaNN/AlloyDB (paradigm ceiling M73/M82 stands) — a recall-stable-under-selective-label-filter result (with a large QPS bonus)
synthetic well-separated clusters (recall meaningful); inline-vs-post is same-data so valid regardless; single run
the absolute recall 1.00 is easy-data-favored (on-centroid queries + well-separated clusters); the load-bearing result is the +0.48 DELTA vs post-filter on the SAME data, not the perfect 1.00
